section.sectionSummaryBrief: Introductory heading for the Purim maamar of 5713.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Purim
(Maamar 2)*

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The name "Purim" derives from the "pur" (lot), indicating that the essence of the Purim miracle is the lot itself, not just its outcome.
section.t: "Therefore they called these days Purim, after the name of the pur [lot]."1
And according to what is known2
that the name of every thing indicates its essence,
it is understood
that the fact that they called these days Purim after the name of the pur is because the main aspect of the festival of Purim is the lot
(pur means the lot3).
And it needs to be understood
(as is pointed out in Torah Or, discourse "Zeh"4),
for at first glance,
this was not
[the main5]
the miracle.
And furthermore,
the lot that Haman cast
(not only was this not the miracle,
but on the contrary)
was part of the decree
[and in the language of the Megillah6:
"He cast a pur, that is the lot, to destroy them and annihilate them"],
and from the fact that these days are called Purim after the name of the pur,
it implies that this
(the lot)
is the main aspect of the Purim miracle,
to the extent that the miracle is named after this.
And at first glance, it could be explained according to what is stated in the Gemara7
that when the lot fell in the month of Adar, [Haman] rejoiced
(Haman)
with great joy,
saying, "A lot has fallen for me in the month in which Moshe died,"
and he did not know that on the seventh of Adar he died and on the seventh of Adar he was born.
And based on this, it could be said
that the reason these days are called after the name of the pur is because the miracle of Purim was that the lot fell in the month of Adar,
the month in which Moshe, the savior of Israel, was born.
But this explanation is still difficult,
because from the fact that the festival is called Purim after the name of the pur,
it implies
that the connection of the miracle to the pur is
(not only to the fact that the lot fell in the month of Adar,
but also)
to the matter of the pur itself.
And on the contrary,
the main miracle was from the aspect of the pur, which is the lot.
For a lot is a very lofty matter,
from which the miracle is drawn.
And that the lot fell on the month of Adar, in which the savior of Israel was born, is
(like all the matters that occurred in the Purim miracle,
which are)
a result of its main essence,
Purim after the name of the pur.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Purim and Yom Kippur are connected through the concept of the lot, both revealing a level above the name Havayah.
section.t: And this will be understood based on what is explained in Torah Or8
that Purim and Yom HaKippurim are related to each other9.
For the explanation of Yom K.
Purim is like Purim
[and moreover,
from the fact that Yom HaKippurim is "k'Purim"
(with only the comparative letter kaf),
it is proven
that Purim is loftier than Yom Kippur10].
And the connection between Yom Kippur and Purim is,
that in both there is the matter of the lot.
For on Yom Kippur they cast a lot upon the two goats11,
and also Purim is named after the pur, which is the lot.
And another matter in the connection of Purim and Yom Kippur,
that both are above the name Havayah12.
For regarding Yom Kippur it is written13
"Before Havayah you shall be purified,"
[meaning] above Havayah14.
And also regarding Purim it is known15
that the reason the name Havayah is not mentioned in the entire Megillat Esther16
is because in Purim there is a revelation of Ein Sof that is above Havayah.
